doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Riverside and the New York scene
title: Recording dates and his own groups in 1958-59
summary: Ware records constantly for Riverside, leads groups in Brooklyn, and does not travel out of New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The period after you had gotten sick and the band broke up, you went back with Miles -- and then what did you do?

Well, I started working in gigs of my own -- maybe that was about '57 or '58, and all of '58 I was recording with different people; Clifford Jordan, John Jenkins Jacob, Hank Mobley -- did a whole lot of dates with him --

I was working out in Brooklyn with my own group, and I walked up on the gig, playing drums - Brooklyn - but before then I was working out of the Continental at a club with my own group; the picture on the back of the Chicago Sound, that was taken in that club by a fellow called [Selly] Copeland, he was a male nurse who just happened to take that photo And I think he sold it to Keepnews to put on the album. But anyway, I was working out there, and I used with Duke Jordan on piano and I forget who was on drums, to have the gigs pretty regular, and then Candido came out here, and I worked for him out there. Well, a lot of those gigs were -- Philly Joe Fergie and Cannonball and myself and Nat Adderley, Milton Kelly, and we had a couple of jobs in the Bronx, all kinds of little gigs, you know, and like I say, we did record dates. I was on call at Riverside, and I was still recording on an average of 4 or 5 dates sometimes a week.
No, no. During this period, I wasn't traveling nowhere, you know. Nowhere at all. I stayed right there in New York City - just did record dates and club dates, you know, and that was it.
And you stayed there ... this was '59, '60 and on up through that period into the sixties?
